newNodes.name: Out-marriage between bands
newNodes.emerged: ~34 kya Sunghir (Russia): genomes of the buried show no close inbreeding, so mates came from a wide network; out-marriage is near-universal among recorded foragers
newNodes.prereqRationale: gift_exchange: the partners who pass shell and stone between bands are the same networks through which spouses are exchanged.
newNodes.rationale: gift_exchange: the partners who pass shell and stone between bands are the same networks through which spouses are exchanged.
newNodes.desc: Young people must marry outside their own band. Every family then has in-laws in other bands, and when its own country fails it can go and live with them.
newNodes.effectRationale: Affines in other bands are a refuge in a local famine: families move to their in-laws' country instead of starving in place.
newNodes.distinctFrom: seasonal_aggregation is the yearly meeting where matches can be made; this is the rule that spouses must come from outside the band. oath_alliance (A2) is a political league of communities that may be sealed by marriage.

newNodes.name: Initiation of the young
newNodes.emerged: ~15 kya adolescent footprints in the deep chambers of Tuc d'Audoubert and Niaux (initiation is one reading); initiation of youths is recorded in nearly every Australian and African forager society
newNodes.prereqRationale: oral_tradition: the lore taught to initiates is the memorised body of songs and stories. shamanic_ritual: ritual specialists conduct the seclusion and the rite.
newNodes.rationale: oral_tradition: the lore taught to initiates is the memorised body of songs and stories. shamanic_ritual: ritual specialists conduct the seclusion and the rite.
newNodes.desc: At puberty boys and girls are secluded with elders, taught the band's tracking, plant and animal lore and its rules, and come back as adults.
newNodes.effectRationale: Adult skills in tracking, trapping and fishing are taught to every youth in a set course, so the band's hunters and fishers are better trained.
newNodes.distinctFrom: oral_tradition keeps the lore; initiation is the institution that transmits it to each cohort. age_sets (A2) turn initiation cohorts into lifelong graded bodies with military and political roles.

newNodes.name: Division of labour by sex and age
newNodes.emerged: ~30 kya Upper Palaeolithic: plant grinding (Bilancino, Pavlov) beside specialised projectile hunting; Kuhn and Stiner (2006) argue a sexual division of foraging work arose with modern humans
newNodes.prereqRationale: atlatl: specialised long-range hunting gear for one task group. grinding_stone: plant-processing gear for the other; the split needs both kits.
newNodes.rationale: atlatl: specialised long-range hunting gear for one task group. grinding_stone: plant-processing gear for the other; the split needs both kits.
newNodes.desc: Men hunt large game far from camp while women, children and elders gather plants, trap small animals and process food. Each household draws on both.
newNodes.effectRationale: A broader, two-track diet means a failed hunt is carried by gathered staples, so households absorb shortfalls they could not before.
newNodes.distinctFrom: food_sharing_norms divides the food once it is brought in; this assigns who goes out for which food. craft_specialists (A2) is specialisation by household and trade, not by sex and age within each household.

newNodes.name: Hunt leaders
newNodes.emerged: ~20 kya Amvrosievka (Ukraine) bison drive-and-kill site and Solutré horse kills; Plains 'buffalo police' who commanded the communal hunt recorded ethnographically
newNodes.prereqRationale: kin_council: the household heads choose the leader for the season. atlatl: the spear-thrower is the weapon of the communal drive.
newNodes.rationale: kin_council: the household heads choose the leader for the season. atlatl: the spear-thrower is the weapon of the communal drive.
newNodes.desc: For the great autumn drive the bands choose a leader whose orders bind everyone; anyone who startles the herd early is punished. After the kill and drying of meat his authority lapses.
newNodes.effectRationale: A disciplined mass kill yields a surplus of dried meat that is stored to carry the band through winter, so stores cover more of the year.
newNodes.distinctFrom: prestige_leadership is voluntary following that anyone may leave; the hunt leader's command is binding but lasts only for the drive. war_band raids other groups; this organises a food harvest.

newNodes.name: Bridewealth
newNodes.emerged: ~6,000 BCE inferred with cattle and sheep herding (ethnographic analogy: Nuer cattle, Zulu lobola); first written as terhatum in the Laws of Eshnunna ~1,800 BCE
newNodes.prereqRationale: cattle OR sheep_goat: livestock is the usual currency of the payment. kin_council: the elders of both lineages negotiate and witness it.
newNodes.rationale: cattle OR sheep_goat: livestock is the usual currency of the payment. kin_council: the elders of both lineages negotiate and witness it.
newNodes.desc: The groom's kin give livestock to the bride's kin. The payment makes the marriage and gives the children to the father's lineage, which must then feed and protect them.
newNodes.effectRationale: Children whose bridewealth has been paid have a whole lineage answerable for them, so in hunger they are fed by uncles and cousins as well as parents.
newNodes.distinctFrom: oath_alliance binds whole communities politically; bridewealth is the transfer between two lineages that creates one marriage. family_law (A3) is the later written law of marriage and inheritance.

newNodes.name: Age sets
newNodes.emerged: ~3,000 BCE inferred with the East African pastoral Neolithic (ethnographic analogy); recorded among the Maasai and Nuer and in the Oromo gada system
newNodes.prereqRationale: cattle: the age-set system is a herding society's way of guarding herds on distant pastures. war_band: the warrior grade grows out of the raiding party.
newNodes.rationale: cattle: the age-set system is a herding society's way of guarding herds on distant pastures. war_band: the warrior grade grows out of the raiding party.
newNodes.desc: Youths initiated together form a set for life. The set serves as warriors guarding herds and camps, then rises together to married men and to ruling elders.
newNodes.effectRationale: The warrior grade lives in outlying cattle camps and patrols the edges of the range, so armed parties see much further around them.
newNodes.distinctFrom: initiation_rites (A1) is a single passage into adulthood; age sets keep each cohort as a standing body that moves through graded duties. war_band is raised for one raid; the warrior grade is permanent.

newNodes.name: Extended-family households
newNodes.emerged: ~5,500 BCE LBK longhouses up to 40 m long, each housing several related couples; matrilineal longhouses recorded among the Iroquois
newNodes.prereqRationale: timber_frame: long post-built houses can shelter several couples under one roof. cereal_cultivation: farming rewards keeping several workers in one household.
newNodes.rationale: timber_frame: long post-built houses can shelter several couples under one roof. cereal_cultivation: farming rewards keeping several workers in one household.
newNodes.desc: Parents, married sons or daughters and their children live in one long house under its senior couple, sharing hearths, stores and labour.
newNodes.effectRationale: Several related couples share one large dwelling, so the same housing stock holds more people.
newNodes.distinctFrom: work_parties call on neighbours from other households; here several couples form one household. household_land_tenure governs fields, not residence.

newNodes.name: Sodalities
newNodes.emerged: ~9,500 BCE Göbekli Tepe and ~8,000 BCE Nevalı Çori enclosures, read by their excavators as meeting places of cult societies (interpretation); kiva societies and Plains soldier societies recorded ethnographically
newNodes.prereqRationale: communal_feasts: the societies meet and recruit at the great feasts. kin_council: they cut across the kin groups whose heads sit in the council.
newNodes.rationale: communal_feasts: the societies meet and recruit at the great feasts. kin_council: they cut across the kin groups whose heads sit in the council.
newNodes.desc: Men's and women's societies recruit across lineages and villages. Members keep a lodge, hold rites and police camps, and a member is received by his society in any village where it meets.
newNodes.effectRationale: A member travelling or moving is lodged and protected by his society in distant villages, so migrants can go further.
newNodes.distinctFrom: guest_right protects any peaceful stranger for a short stay; a sodality lodges its own sworn members. megalithic_monuments are the places built; this is the membership organisation itself.

newNodes.name: Stock friendship
newNodes.emerged: ~4,500 BCE inferred with the spread of herding into the Sahara and East Africa (ethnographic analogy); bond-friends who keep each other's cattle recorded among the Turkana, Jie and Maasai
newNodes.prereqRationale: cattle: the animals placed with partners. gift_exchange: the long-distance partnership is the forager exchange tie turned to livestock.
newNodes.rationale: cattle: the animals placed with partners. gift_exchange: the long-distance partnership is the forager exchange tie turned to livestock.
newNodes.desc: A herder places some of his animals with bond-friends in other districts and keeps theirs in return, so drought or disease never takes his whole herd.
newNodes.effectRationale: Herds split between distant partners survive local drought and epidemics, so each herder keeps and breeds more stock.
newNodes.distinctFrom: transhumance moves one's own flock between seasonal pastures; stock friendship spreads ownership risk across partners. bridewealth moves animals once to make a marriage.

newNodes.name: Fishing-station rights
newNodes.emerged: ~6,000 BCE Mesolithic fish weirs on the Liffey (Dublin) rebuilt on the same spot for centuries; kin-owned fishing stations recorded on the Northwest Coast
newNodes.prereqRationale: basketry: weirs and traps are wattle work. dugout: the station is reached and worked by boat.
newNodes.rationale: basketry: weirs and traps are wattle work. dugout: the station is reached and worked by boat.
newNodes.desc: A kin group owns a named weir or fishing place and keeps it in repair. Others fish there only by its leave, so the weir is worth rebuilding every year.
newNodes.effectRationale: Secure ownership makes it worthwhile to build and maintain fixed weirs and traps, which take far more fish than line and spear.
newNodes.distinctFrom: band_territories (A1) holds a whole foraging range; this is property in one fixed fishing installation. household_land_tenure covers fields, not waters.

newNodes.name: Inviolable seed corn
newNodes.emerged: ~9,500 BCE purpose-built grain stores at Jerf el-Ahmar and Dhra'; keeping seed back from eating is the precondition of domestication, and peasant custom treats it as untouchable
newNodes.prereqRationale: cereal_domesticated: domestic cereals exist only because seed was kept back and replanted. kin_council: the elders enforce the rule against eating it.
newNodes.rationale: cereal_domesticated: domestic cereals exist only because seed was kept back and replanted. kin_council: the elders enforce the rule against eating it.
newNodes.desc: Next year's seed is set aside at harvest and may not be eaten even in hunger. The best ears are kept for it, so every planting starts from good seed.
newNodes.effectRationale: A protected store of selected seed raises the next crop; this is the stored-seed bonus the granary operand models.
newNodes.distinctFrom: communal_storage is a famine reserve to be eaten in need; seed corn is the one store that must not be eaten. grain_storage is the building, not the rule.

newNodes.name: Rights of clearance
newNodes.emerged: ~5,500 BCE inferred for early farmers clearing the European forest; recorded among swidden farmers of Africa, Southeast Asia and Amazonia (the clearer holds the plot while it is cropped)
newNodes.prereqRationale: ground_stone_early: the ground axe fells the trees. cereal_cultivation: the cleared plot is sown.
newNodes.rationale: ground_stone_early: the ground axe fells the trees. cereal_cultivation: the cleared plot is sown.
newNodes.desc: Whoever clears a plot from the forest holds it while he crops it. When it is left to regrow it returns to the lineage, and any member may clear it again.
newNodes.effectRationale: Households may open new plots further out without asking for an allotment, so the settlement farms a wider area.
newNodes.distinctFrom: household_land_tenure gives permanent heritable fields; clearance gives temporary use of forest plots. first_settler_rights is allotment by the founding lineage, not a right earned by clearing.

newNodes.name: Investment partnerships
newNodes.emerged: ~1,900 BCE Kanesh (Kültepe) tablets: Old Assyrian naruqqum 'money-bag' partnerships, investors pooling gold for a merchant for ten years or more
newNodes.prereqRationale: trade: the long-distance caravan trade the fund finances. hacksilver: capital is pooled and reckoned in weighed metal.
newNodes.rationale: trade: the long-distance caravan trade the fund finances. hacksilver: capital is pooled and reckoned in weighed metal.
newNodes.desc: Several investors pool gold in one 'bag' entrusted to a travelling merchant for years. He trades with it, they share the profit, and the capital stays at work between caravans.
newNodes.effectRationale: Standing pooled capital lets merchants buy stocks where they are cheap and move them to market without waiting to raise funds for each trip.
newNodes.distinctFrom: interest_bearing_credit lends at a fixed rate; investors in a naruqqum share profit and loss. commenda (A6) funds one voyage; the naruqqum is a long-term fund across many caravans.

newNodes.name: Court upbringing of vassal heirs
newNodes.emerged: ~1,450 BCE Thutmose III brings the sons of Levantine rulers to be raised in the Egyptian royal nursery (kap) and sends them home as vassal kings
newNodes.prereqRationale: royal_envoys: the princes come as part of the diplomatic exchange with vassal courts. scribal_schools: they are educated alongside court children in the palace school.
newNodes.rationale: royal_envoys: the princes come as part of the diplomatic exchange with vassal courts. scribal_schools: they are educated alongside court children in the palace school.
newNodes.desc: Sons of subject kings are brought to the great king's palace, schooled with his own children and sent back to rule when their fathers die.
newNodes.effectRationale: Vassal rulers raised at court know its language and officials and owe it their thrones, so royal authority holds in distant subject lands.
newNodes.distinctFrom: dynastic_marriage ties houses by marriage; here the heirs themselves are raised at court. scribal_schools train officials, not foreign rulers.

newNodes.name: Royal road-houses
newNodes.emerged: ~2,090 BCE Shulgi of Ur claims to have built road-houses with gardens and wells along the highways; Ur III way-station accounts record rations to travellers
newNodes.prereqRationale: appointed_officials: the stations are staffed and provisioned by officials. donkey: the pack animals they rest and fodder.
newNodes.rationale: appointed_officials: the stations are staffed and provisioned by officials. donkey: the pack animals they rest and fodder.
newNodes.desc: The crown builds staffed rest-houses a day's march apart on the main roads, with water, fodder and food for official travellers and caravans.
newNodes.effectRationale: Travellers find water, food and fresh fodder at every stage instead of carrying them, so they cover more ground each day.
newNodes.distinctFrom: campaign_provisioning stocks depots for one army's march; road-houses are permanent stations for all official travel. royal_post (A4) is a courier relay, not lodging.

newNodes.name: Herding contracts
newNodes.emerged: ~2,050 BCE Ur III herding accounts fix lambing and wool quotas for temple flocks; Laws of Hammurabi §261-267 (~1,754 BCE) regulate hired herdsmen
newNodes.prereqRationale: temple_economy: temple and palace own large flocks that must be entrusted to herdsmen. wool: the quotas are reckoned in fleeces and lambs.
newNodes.rationale: temple_economy: temple and palace own large flocks that must be entrusted to herdsmen. wool: the quotas are reckoned in fleeces and lambs.
newNodes.desc: Temple and palace flocks are entrusted to herdsmen under contract: a fixed number of lambs and weight of wool per hundred ewes, an allowance for losses, and the surplus is theirs.
newNodes.effectRationale: Quotas with a share of the surplus give herdsmen a stake in breeding and fleece, so each herder delivers more.
newNodes.distinctFrom: hire_tariffs fix day wages for hired work; herding contracts set yield quotas on entrusted flocks. stock_friendship (A2) swaps animals between equal owners for insurance.

newNodes.name: Peace of God
newNodes.emerged: 989 CE Council of Charroux; 1,027 CE Truce of God at Toulouges: bishops forbid violence against peasants, clergy and their goods on pain of excommunication
newNodes.prereqRationale: feudal_monarchy: the private wars of castellans that the movement restrains. monasticism: Cluniac monks led the peace councils.
newNodes.rationale: feudal_monarchy: the private wars of castellans that the movement restrains. monasticism: Cluniac monks led the peace councils.
newNodes.desc: Church councils forbid knights to attack peasants, clergy, mills or oxen, and ban fighting on holy days, enforcing it with excommunication and sworn peace leagues.
newNodes.effectRationale: Peasants, ploughing oxen and mills are spared in private wars, so farm work goes on through feuds that once stripped the fields.
newNodes.distinctFrom: pilgrimage (A4) protects travellers to a festival; the Peace of God protects farmers and their tools from local war. holy_war_doctrine redirects violence outward; this restrains it at home.

newNodes.name: Parish tithe
newNodes.emerged: 779 CE Capitulary of Herstal makes the tithe compulsory across the Frankish realm; tithe barns built across Europe from ~1,100 CE
newNodes.prereqRationale: state_religion: a church established by the crown can have its levy enforced by royal law. taxation: assessment of a share of the harvest already exists.
newNodes.rationale: state_religion: a church established by the crown can have its levy enforced by royal law. taxation: assessment of a share of the harvest already exists.
newNodes.desc: Every household owes a tenth of its grain and young stock to its parish church. The tenth is gathered in the tithe barn to keep the clergy, the church and the parish poor.
newNodes.effectRationale: A tenth of every harvest is held in barns in each parish, so the district keeps larger stores against bad years.
newNodes.distinctFrom: taxation is the ruler's levy; the tithe is a separate church levy collected parish by parish. temple_economy (A3) is a temple running its own estates, not a levy on everyone's harvest.

newNodes.name: Sharecropping contracts
newNodes.emerged: ~800 CE muzāraʿa and musāqāt sharecropping contracts in the Islamic law books; ~1,250 CE Tuscan mezzadria
newNodes.prereqRationale: commercial_law: the contract forms of the jurists, which also govern these agrarian partnerships. plough_ard: the plough team the owner usually supplies.
newNodes.rationale: commercial_law: the contract forms of the jurists, which also govern these agrarian partnerships. plough_ard: the plough team the owner usually supplies.
newNodes.desc: A landowner provides land, seed and plough oxen; a free tenant family provides labour, and the harvest is split by agreed shares.
newNodes.effectRationale: The owner's plough team and tools go to the family working the land, so tenants who could not afford them farm with full equipment.
newNodes.distinctFrom: manorialism binds tenants with labour dues; sharecropping is a free contract that splits the crop. commenda pairs capital and labour for one trading voyage, not a farm season. tenancy_protection (A9) later protects these tenants.

newNodes.name: Bridge trusts
newNodes.emerged: ~1,177 CE Pont Saint-Bénézet, Avignon, built by a bridge brotherhood; 1,282 CE London Bridge House estate; 1,399 CE Rochester Bridge Trust
newNodes.prereqRationale: bridge_stone: the masonry spans the trusts build and keep. monasticism: the brotherhoods and alms that fund them are a religious form of endowment.
newNodes.rationale: bridge_stone: the masonry spans the trusts build and keep. monasticism: the brotherhoods and alms that fund them are a religious form of endowment.
newNodes.desc: Brotherhoods and endowed trusts raise alms, rents and bequests to build stone bridges and keep them in repair forever, with wardens who answer for the fund.
newNodes.effectRationale: Permanent bridges replace fords and ferries that were closed in flood or slow to cross, so overland journeys go faster.
newNodes.distinctFrom: public_hospitals are endowed for care of the sick; bridge trusts for crossings. turnpike_trusts (A7) fund roads from tolls, not alms and endowment. forest_law and water_boards manage resources, not transport works.

newNodes.name: Crop insurance
newNodes.emerged: 1,938 CE US Federal Crop Insurance Act; ~1,985 CE India's Comprehensive Crop Insurance Scheme
newNodes.prereqRationale: probability_statistics: premiums are priced on yield records. cooperatives: the first crop and hail insurers were farmers' mutuals.
newNodes.rationale: probability_statistics: premiums are priced on yield records. cooperatives: the first crop and hail insurers were farmers' mutuals.
newNodes.desc: Farmers pay a premium each season and are compensated when drought, flood or hail cuts their yield below an insured level.
newNodes.effectRationale: Payouts arrive in the bad year itself, so farm households absorb a crop failure instead of selling stock and land.
newNodes.distinctFrom: price_support guarantees a price for what is harvested; insurance pays when there is no harvest. deposit_insurance protects bank savings, not crops.

newNodes.name: Land titling
newNodes.emerged: ~1,984 CE Thailand Land Titling Project; 1,996 CE Peru's COFOPRI registers titles for urban squatter settlements
newNodes.prereqRationale: land_registry: titles are entered in a public register. civil_code: codified property law defines what a title secures.
newNodes.rationale: land_registry: titles are entered in a public register. civil_code: codified property law defines what a title secures.
newNodes.desc: The state surveys plots held by custom or occupation and issues registered titles to the families who live on and work them.
newNodes.effectRationale: Families with secure title invest in solid walls and roofs instead of temporary shelters, so their homes last longer.
newNodes.distinctFrom: land_reform redistributes land; titling secures what people already hold. indigenous_land_rights restores collective title; this issues individual titles. tenancy_protection secures tenants, not owners.

newNodes.name: Community forestry
newNodes.emerged: ~1,978 CE Nepal hands forests to panchayats; 1,990 CE India's Joint Forest Management; 1,993 CE Nepal Forest Act creates community forest user groups
newNodes.prereqRationale: nature_conservation: the state already reserves forests for protection. cooperatives: user groups manage the forest as a member association.
newNodes.rationale: nature_conservation: the state already reserves forests for protection. cooperatives: user groups manage the forest as a member association.
newNodes.desc: The state hands degraded forests to village user groups, which set harvest rules, guard the woods and share timber, fodder and firewood among members.
newNodes.effectRationale: Guarded forests regrow and are cut by plan, so timber yields rise; user groups allot members cheap timber for house repair.
newNodes.distinctFrom: forest_law (A6) reserves woods for the crown; community forestry hands them to villagers. fisheries_management sets catch quotas by the state, not by local users.

newNodes.name: Land consolidation
newNodes.emerged: 1,953 CE West German Flurbereinigungsgesetz; 1,954 CE Dutch land consolidation act; consolidation programmes across Europe and Asia in the following decades
newNodes.prereqRationale: mechanised_agriculture: tractors and combines need large regular fields. land_registry: holdings must be registered before they can be exchanged.
newNodes.rationale: mechanised_agriculture: tractors and combines need large regular fields. land_registry: holdings must be registered before they can be exchanged.
newNodes.desc: Officials redraw a district's scattered strips into compact holdings of equal value, with new field roads and drains, so each farm works a few large fields.
newNodes.effectRationale: Machines lose little time turning and travelling between large compact fields, so equipped farmers get more from their tools.
newNodes.distinctFrom: land_reform changes who owns land; consolidation rearranges plots among the same owners. zoning regulates urban use.

newNodes.name: Rural electrification
newNodes.emerged: 1,920 CE Soviet GOELRO plan; 1,935 CE US Rural Electrification Administration lends to farmers' power cooperatives
newNodes.prereqRationale: ac_transmission: long high-voltage lines reach scattered farms. cooperatives: rural power was built by member cooperatives on public loans.
newNodes.rationale: ac_transmission: long high-voltage lines reach scattered farms. cooperatives: rural power was built by member cooperatives on public loans.
newNodes.desc: The state lends to cooperatives and utilities to run power lines out to villages and farms that private companies would not serve.
newNodes.effectRationale: Electric pumps lift groundwater for irrigation in dry spells, so harvests vary less from year to year.
newNodes.distinctFrom: electricity_generation and ac_transmission are the technologies; this is the programme that extends them to rural areas. universal_telephone_service does the same for telephones. river_basin_authority builds dams, not distribution lines.

newNodes.name: Child nutrition programmes
newNodes.emerged: 1,975 CE India's Integrated Child Development Services (village anganwadi centres); 1,982 CE UNICEF's growth-monitoring drive
newNodes.prereqRationale: epidemiology: weighing and measuring children identifies who is malnourished. oral_rehydration: diarrhoea treatment is part of the same village package.
newNodes.rationale: epidemiology: weighing and measuring children identifies who is malnourished. oral_rehydration: diarrhoea treatment is part of the same village package.
newNodes.desc: Village centres weigh young children every month and give supplementary food to the underweight and to pregnant and nursing mothers.
newNodes.effectRationale: Under-fives at risk are found early and fed, so fewer young children die when food runs short.
newNodes.distinctFrom: school_meals feed pupils at school; this reaches children under school age and their mothers. primary_health_care treats illness; this monitors growth and feeds.

newNodes.name: Employment guarantee
newNodes.emerged: 1,972 CE Maharashtra Employment Guarantee Scheme during the drought; 2,005 CE India's National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (100 days of work a year on demand)
newNodes.prereqRationale: income_tax: the guarantee is paid from general revenue. mass_suffrage: rural voters made work on demand a legal right.
newNodes.rationale: income_tax: the guarantee is paid from general revenue. mass_suffrage: rural voters made work on demand a legal right.
newNodes.desc: Any rural adult who asks for work must be given paid unskilled work on local public projects within a fortnight, or receive an allowance.
newNodes.effectRationale: When harvests fail, labourers claim wages at once instead of migrating or starving; the Maharashtra scheme carried millions through the 1972 drought.
newNodes.distinctFrom: public_works_relief hires the unemployed when the state chooses; the guarantee is a right claimed by the worker. unemployment_insurance pays insured wage earners, not rural labourers.

newNodes.name: Livestock disease campaigns
newNodes.emerged: 1,924 CE Office International des Épizooties founded; 1,994 CE Global Rinderpest Eradication Programme; rinderpest declared eradicated 2,011 CE
newNodes.prereqRationale: vaccine_lab: the vaccines the campaigns deliver. international_organizations: a standing international office coordinates reporting and eradication.
newNodes.rationale: vaccine_lab: the vaccines the campaigns deliver. international_organizations: a standing international office coordinates reporting and eradication.
newNodes.desc: Public veterinary services and an international office track cattle plagues, vaccinate herds and control movement until diseases like rinderpest are wiped out.
newNodes.effectRationale: Herds no longer die in plague years, so each herder keeps and raises far more stock.
newNodes.distinctFrom: expanded_immunization vaccinates people; this vaccinates herds. agricultural_extension advises on crops and methods, not on animal disease control.

findings: Scope: 28 new civics to lift the finite civics count from 449 to 477 (about 93 % of 515 technologies). By Age: A1 +4, A2 +8, A3 +4, A6 +4, A9 +8.

Every node was checked against all existing and tranche-2 new nodes, including the reviewer's merge and drop verdicts. Ideas the reviewer had already merged were not proposed again: storehouse sealing, stinted commons, pious endowments, transit authorities and free-movement areas.

Effects favour under-used operands: granaries.farmYieldBonusMax, consumption.granaryYearsOfDemand, housing.personsPerDwelling, housing.upkeepTimberPerDwellingYear, production.toolYieldBonusMax, production.outputPerHerderPerYear, fog.formationSightNodes and roads.baselineKmPerDay. None of the five saturated operands is used. One node, court_upbringing, uses the heavily used governance.authorityDecayCostUnits, because it is the causal operand for loyal vassal courts.

Grounding caveats. age_sets (A2), stock_friendship (A2) and clearance_usufruct (A2) are dated by ethnographic analogy and say so in their emerged text. sodalities rests on an excavators' interpretation of Göbekli Tepe, which is flagged as such. initiation_rites rests on a contested reading of adolescent cave footprints.

Prerequisites use only the 684 existing nodes or this file's own ids. No other author's tranche-2 new id is used. For example, prestige_leadership, interest_bearing_credit and primary_health_care are cited only in distinctFrom.
